parts:
Hi Chris, 

from a quick inspection I think you may have to fix the nimbleRcall, by declaring the type of the arguments in your R functions; since you have 

V_n <- function(lambda, gamma, N) { ...}

you need to specify what are lambda, gamma and N when using nimbleRcall. Assuming the first argument is a vector and the other two scalar you should have something like this: 

RV_n <- nimbleRcall(function(lambda=double(1), gamma=double(0) , N = double(0)){},
                    Rfun='V_n',
                    returnType = double(1))

And I also think you may want to update also the second nimbleRcall:

Rlength_unique <- nimbleRcall(function(vec=double(1)){},
                              Rfun='length_unique',
                              returnType = double(0))


Hope this helps!

Best, 

Sally

Sally, Chris,

It seems this code attempts to implement the mixture of finite mixtures (MFM) approach of Miller and Harrison (https://jwmi.github.io/publications/MFM.pdf). 

I believe that the dMCRP function should be defined on a vector of integers, i.e., we should have 

dMCRP <- nimbleFunction(  
  run=function(x = integer(1),
...

Formally, the restaurant process is a mass function defined for a partition of integers {1, ..., n} e.g., x = (1, 1, 2, 2), for example, if there are two clusters.

In the paper, Miller and Harrison claim:
This is a direct adaptation of “Algorithm 3” for DPMs (MacEachern, 1994; Neal, 1992, 2000). The only differences are that in Algorithm 3, |c| + γ is replaced by |c|, and γVn(t + 1)/Vn(t) is replaced by α (the concentration parameter).

Is it possible to use the code in sampler_CRP to implement this change? I assume not since the normal CRP only has a single hyperparameter (alpha) and is a function of the number of clusters |c|. Here, we would have a second hyperparameter gamma that needs to be included in the sampling scheme.

Sally, Chris,

It seems this code attempts to implement the mixture of finite mixtures (MFM) approach of Miller and Harrison (https://jwmi.github.io/publications/MFM.pdf). 

I believe that the dMCRP function should be defined on a vector of integers, i.e., we should have 

dMCRP <- nimbleFunction(  
  run=function(x = integer(1),
...

Formally, the restaurant process is a mass function defined for a partition of integers {1, ..., n} e.g., x = (1, 1, 2, 2), for example, if there are two clusters.

In the paper, Miller and Harrison claim:
This is a direct adaptation of “Algorithm 3” for DPMs (MacEachern, 1994; Neal, 1992, 2000). The only differences are that in Algorithm 3, |c| + γ is replaced by |c|, and γVn(t + 1)/Vn(t) is replaced by α (the concentration parameter).

Is it possible to use the code in sampler_CRP to implement this change? I assume not since the normal CRP only has a single hyperparameter (alpha) and is a function of the number of clusters |c|. Here, we would have a second hyperparameter gamma that needs to be included in the sampling scheme.

All,

I've put forth my best effort towards implementing the sampler, but I'm a little stuck.

Here's what I have done so far:
  1. Implemented dMCRP (NOTE: it will only compile if you give the input argument as a vector of doubles--does not work as a vector of integers. Hopefully, this will not cause a problem since ultimately we will be sampling the z's
  2. Created invalid rMCRP function because Nimble complained
  3. Confirmed with 3-dim case that summing over dMCRP evaluates to 1 (so the normalizing constant is computed correctly)
  4. Wrote some nimbleCode that uses the custom density function
  5. Started writing the sampler based on Neal Algorithm 8 (I realize the current example is a conjugate case, but I wanted to write the non-conjugate case for generality)

What needs to be done (highlighted below in the code):
  1. Compute the log conditional density for y_i | z_i (non-conjugate case)
  2. Sample from the base measure for the auxiliary variables for Neal Algorithm 8.


library(nimble)
remove(list = ls())
logsumexp <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(a = double(0), b = double(0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    m <- max(a, b)
    return( log(exp(a-m) + exp(b-m)) + m )
  }
)

logsumexp_vec <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    m <- max(x)
    return( m + log(sum(exp(x - m))) )
  }
)

#' Compute log V_n(t) as in Miller and Harrison
#'
#' @param t number of partitions
#' @param n sample size
#' @param lambda mean hyperparameter for poisson prior on k-1
#' @param gamma dirichlet parameter
#' @param tol tolerance for sum
#' @return computation of log V_n(t)
logvn <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
      t      = integer(0)
    , n      = integer(0)
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma  = double(0)
    , tol    = double(0, default = 1e-12)
  ) {
    returnType(double(0))
    thresh <- 1.0 - tol     ## the sum decays faster than the poisson CDF
    ## Number of partitions t must be <= n
    if ( t > n )
      return(-Inf)
    a <- 0.0      ## Previous value of log V_n(t)
    c <- -Inf     ## Computation of log V_n(t)
    k <- 1        ## counter for the sum
    p <- 0.0      ## poisson CDF calculation (to be compared with thresh)
    while ( abs(a-c) > tol | p < thresh ) {
      if ( k >= t ) {
        gamma_k <- gamma * k
        a       <- c
        b       <- lgamma(k+1) - lgamma(k-t+1) - lgamma(gamma_k + n) + lgamma(gamma_k) + dpois(k-1, lambda, 1)
        c       <- logsumexp(a, b)
      }
      p <- p + dpois(k-1, lambda, 0)
      k <- k + 1
    }
    return(c)
  }
)

nimbleUnique <- nimbleRcall(
  prototype   = function(x = double(1)) {}
  , Rfun       = "unique"
  , returnType = double(1)
)
getClusterSize <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(x = double(1)) {
    returnType(double(1))
    clusters    <- nimbleUnique(x)
    nclusters   <- length(clusters)
    clusterSize <- rep(0, nclusters)
    n <- length(x)
    for ( i in 1:n ) {
      for ( j in 1:nclusters ) {
        if ( x[i] == clusters[j] ) {
          clusterSize[j] <- clusterSize[j] + 1
        }
      }
    }
    return(clusterSize)
  }
)

dMCRP <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
      x = double(1)
    , size = integer(0)
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma = double(0)
    , tol = double(0, default = 1e-12)
    , log = integer(0, default = 0)
  ) {
    returnType(double(0))
    C <- getClusterSize(x) ## size of each partition
    t <- length(C)         ## number of parts in the partition
    ## Compute log V_n(t)
    log_vn <- logvn(t, size, lambda, gamma, tol)
    ## Compute log kernel of mass function
    logK <- 0
    ## Compute lgamma(gamma)
    lgamma_gamma <- lgamma(gamma)
    for ( j in 1:t ) {
      logK <- logK + lgamma(gamma + C[j]) - lgamma_gamma
    }
    if ( log )
      return( logK + log_vn )
    return( exp( logK + log_vn ) )
  }
)

rMCRP <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
      n = integer(0)
    , size = integer(0)
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma = double(0)
    , tol = double(0, default = 1e-12)
  ) {
    returnType(double(1))
    return(rep(1, size))
  }
)

## test n = 3 case
x <- cbind( c(1, 1, 1), c(1, 1, 2), c(1, 2, 2), c(1, 2, 1), c(1, 2, 3) )
sum( apply(x, 2, dMCRP, size = 3, lambda = 3, gamma = 2) )  ## sums to 1

code <- nimbleCode({
  lambda ~ dgamma(0.1, 0.1)
  gamma  ~ dgamma(0.1, 0.1)
  z[1:n] ~ dMCRP(size = n, lambda, gamma, tol = 1e-12)
  nclust <- length( nimbleUnique(z[1:n]) )
  for ( k in 1:Kmax ) {
    mu[k] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 5)
  }
  for ( i in 1:n ) {
    y[i] ~ dnorm(mu[z[i]], 1)
  }
})

sampler_MFM <- nimbleFunction(
  name = 'sampler_MFM',
  contains = sampler_BASE,
  setup = function(model, mvSaved, target, control) {
    targetElements <- model$expandNodeNames(target, returnScalarComponents = TRUE)
    targetVar      <- model$getVarNames(nodes = target)
    n              <- length(targetElements)
    naux           <- control$naux
    parms          <- model$getParents(target)
    lambda         <- values(model, parms[1])[1]
    gamma          <- values(model, parms[2])[1]
    depvar         <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE, dataOnly = TRUE, stochOnly = TRUE)
    if (is.null(control$naux))
      naux <- 3
    znew <- 1:n
    for ( j in 1:n ) {
      ## Remove observation j
      if ( j == 1 ) {
        z_mj <- z[2:n]
      } else if ( j == n ) {
        z_mj <- z[1:(n-1)]
      } else {
        z_mj <- z[c(1:j-1, (j+1):n)]
      }
      clustSize_mj  <- getClusterSize(z_mj)    ## number in each cluster after taking away obs j
      k_mj          <- length(clustSize_mj)    ## number of clusters after taking away obs j
      h_mj          <- nclust_mj + aux         ## number of total parameters incl. auxiliary
      logProbs_mj   <- rep(0, nclust_mj + h)   ## placeholder for log probabilities
      log_vn_tplus1 <- logvn(k_mj + 1)
      log_vn_t      <- logvn(k_mj)
      alpha_mj      <- exp( log(gamma) + log_vn_tplus1 - log_vn_t ) ## concentration parameter
      ## loop through number of clusters + aux variables
      for ( k in 1:k_mj ) {
        ## REPLACE ... WITH LOG LIKELIHOOD BASED ON THIS CLUSTER AND DEPVAR[j]
        logprobs_mj[k] <- log(clustSize_mj[k]) - log(n - 1 + alpha_mj) + ...
      }
      for ( k in (k_mj+1):h_mj ) {
        ## REPLACE ... WITH A DRAW FROM BASE MEASURE
        ...
       
        ## REPLACE ... WITH LOG LIKELIHOOD BASED ON THIS CLUSTER AND DEPVAR[j]
        logprobs_mj[k] <- log(alpha_mj) - log(naux) - log(n - 1 + alpha_mj) + ...
      }
      znew[j] <- rcat( n = 1, prob = exp(logprobs_mj) )
    }
    model[[target]] <<- znew
    model$calculate(target)
    nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = target, logProb = TRUE)
  }
)


## SAMPLE DATA
n <- 20
K <- 2
z <- rbinom(n, 1, 0.5)
y <- numeric(n)
y[z==1] <- rnorm(sum(z==1), 2, 1)
y[z==0] <- rnorm(sum(z==0), -2, 1)
Kmax <- 5
mod <- nimbleModel(
  code
  , constants = list(n = n, Kmax = Kmax)
  , data  = list('y' = y)
  , inits = list('z' = rep(1, n), 'mu' = rnorm(Kmax, mean = 0, sd = 0.5), 'lambda' = 1, 'gamma' = 1)
)
cmod <- compileNimble(mod)
conf <- configureMCMC(mod, monitors = c('nclust', 'lambda', 'gamma', 'mu'))

It seems this code attempts to implement the mixture of finite mixtures (MFM) approach of Miller and Harrison (https://jwmi.github.io/publications/MFM.pdf).

Formally, the restaurant process is a mass function defined for a partition of integers {1, ..., n} e.g., x = (1, 1, 2, 2), for example, if there are two clusters.

This is a direct adaptation of “Algorithm 3” for DPMs (MacEachern, 1994; Neal, 1992, 2000). The only differences are that in Algorithm 3, |c| + γ is replaced by |c|, and γVn(t + 1)/Vn(t) is replaced by α (the concentration parameter).

Hi Ethan,

Looks like you've made some good progress. Here are some suggestions:

1) You'll need your sampler_MFM to have a setup function and a run function. The actual sampling calculations need to be in the run function (this looks like the stuff starting with 'for(j in 1:n)' in your code).
The sampler_CRP code (in BNP_samplers.R) may be helpful, but the setup code there is quite complicated because we need to handle all sorts of model structures a user might pass. So you might also look at some simpler samplers (in MCMC_samplers.R to get a better sense for what is in setup() and what is in run().

2) You'll need a 'reset' method for sampler_MFM. You can just use the 'dummy' one shown for sampler_CRP.

3) As far as the computations, I presume you know what calcs to do for '## REPLACE ... WITH LOG LIKELIHOOD BASED ON THIS CLUSTER AND DEPVAR[j]'.

For ## REPLACE ... WITH A DRAW FROM BASE MEASURE',  you'll need to use the 'simulate' method applied to the cluster parameters for the given cluster. You might be able 
to determine the cluster parameters in the setup code such that this works for any model. We do this in sampler_CRP, but it is complicated graph stuff. So an easier alternative is to have the user of sampler_MFM pass in a vector of the node names for the cluster parameters as part of the control list. Then you can grab those in the setup code and use them in the run code.

4) You'll need to set `z <- model[[target]]` early on in the run code.

5) At the end of run code, you need to make sure that you copy the current values of the model and all logProbs into the mvSaved modelValues (see various samplers for an example of this). This means that you'll also need to make sure that you've updated any deterministic dependencies of any model nodes that you changed in the sampling in sampler_MFM as well as any logProbs for dependencies of any model nodes that you changed (including logProbs of the changed nodes themselves). In sampler_CRP you'll see we do this in the last couple lines of run().

HTH. Happy to iterate further as you work on it.

-chris

#' Compute log V_n(t) as in Miller and Harrison
#'
#' @param t number of partitions
#' @param n sample size
#' @param lambda mean hyperparameter for poisson prior on k-1
#' @param gamma dirichlet parameter
#' @param tol tolerance for sum
#' @return computation of log V_n(t)
logvn <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
      t      = integer(0)
    , n      = integer(0)
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma  = double(0)
    , tol    = double(0, default = 1e-12)
  ) {
    returnType(double(0))
    thresh <- 1.0 - tol     ## the sum decays faster than the poisson CDF
    ## Number of partitions t must be <= n
    if ( t > n )
      return(-Inf)
    a <- 0.0      ## Previous value of log V_n(t)
    c <- -Inf     ## Computation of log V_n(t)
    k <- 1        ## counter for the sum
    p <- 0.0      ## poisson CDF calculation (to be compared with thresh)
    while ( abs(a-c) > tol | p < thresh ) {
      if ( k >= t ) {
        gamma_k <- gamma * k
        a       <- c
        b       <- lgamma(k+1) - lgamma(k-t+1) - lgamma(gamma_k + n) + lgamma(gamma_k) + dpois(k-1, lambda, 1)
        c       <- logsumexp(a, b)
      }
      p <- p + dpois(k-1, lambda, 0)
      k <- k + 1
    }
    return(c)
  }
)

  run = function(x = double(1)) {
    returnType(double(1))
    clusters    <- nimbleUnique(x)
    nclusters   <- length(clusters)

)

  run = function(
      x = double(1)
    , size = integer(0)
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma = double(0)
    , tol = double(0, default = 1e-12)
    , log = integer(0, default = 0)

    returnType(double(0))
    C <- getClusterSize(x) ## size of each partition

    ## Compute log V_n(t)
    log_vn <- logvn(t, size, lambda, gamma, tol)
    ## Compute log kernel of mass function
    logK <- 0
    ## Compute lgamma(gamma)
    lgamma_gamma <- lgamma(gamma)
    for ( j in 1:t ) {
      logK <- logK + lgamma(gamma + C[j]) - lgamma_gamma
    }
    if ( log )
      return( logK + log_vn )
    return( exp( logK + log_vn ) )
  }
)

    , n      = integer(0)
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma  = double(0)
    , tol    = double(0, default = 1e-12)
  ) {
    returnType(double(0))
    thresh <- 1.0 - tol     ## the sum decays faster than the poisson CDF
    ## Number of partitions t must be <= n
    if ( t > n )
      return(-Inf)
    a <- 0.0      ## Previous value of log V_n(t)
    c <- -Inf     ## Computation of log V_n(t)
    k <- 1        ## counter for the sum
    p <- 0.0      ## poisson CDF calculation (to be compared with thresh)
    while ( abs(a-c) > tol | p < thresh ) {
      if ( k >= t ) {
        gamma_k <- gamma * k
        a       <- c
        b       <- lgamma(k+1) - lgamma(k-t+1) - lgamma(gamma_k + n) + lgamma(gamma_k) + dpois(k-1, lambda, 1)
        c       <- logsumexp(a, b)
      }
      p <- p + dpois(k-1, lambda, 0)
      k <- k + 1
    }
    return(c)
  }
)

Sally, Chris,

It seems this code attempts to implement the mixture of finite mixtures (MFM) approach of Miller and Harrison (https://jwmi.github.io/publications/MFM.pdf). 

I believe that the dMCRP function should be defined on a vector of integers, i.e., we should have

Formally, the restaurant process is a mass function defined for a partition of integers {1, ..., n} e.g., x = (1, 1, 2, 2), for example, if there are two clusters.

In the paper, Miller and Harrison claim:
This is a direct adaptation of “Algorithm 3” for DPMs (MacEachern, 1994; Neal, 1992, 2000). The only differences are that in Algorithm 3, |c| + γ is replaced by |c|, and γVn(t + 1)/Vn(t) is replaced by α (the concentration parameter).

#' Compute log V_n(t) as in Miller and Harrison
#'
#' @param t number of partitions
#' @param n sample size
#' @param lambda mean hyperparameter for poisson prior on k-1
#' @param gamma dirichlet parameter
#' @param tol tolerance for sum
#' @return computation of log V_n(t)
logvn <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
      t      = integer(0)
    , n      = integer(0)
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma  = double(0)
    , tol    = double(0, default = 1e-12)
  ) {
    returnType(double(0))
    thresh <- 1.0 - tol     ## the sum decays faster than the poisson CDF
    ## Number of partitions t must be <= n
    if ( t > n )
      return(-Inf)
    a <- 0.0      ## Previous value of log V_n(t)
    c <- -Inf     ## Computation of log V_n(t)
    k <- 1        ## counter for the sum
    p <- 0.0      ## poisson CDF calculation (to be compared with thresh)
    while ( abs(a-c) > tol | p < thresh ) {
      if ( k >= t ) {
        gamma_k <- gamma * k
        a       <- c
        b       <- lgamma(k+1) - lgamma(k-t+1) - lgamma(gamma_k + n) + lgamma(gamma_k) + dpois(k-1, lambda, 1)
        c       <- logsumexp(a, b)
      }
      p <- p + dpois(k-1, lambda, 0)
      k <- k + 1
    }
    return(c)
  }
)

#' Function to get sizes of clusters

n   <- length(x)

res[x[i]] <- res[x[i]] + 1

#'    \item "empty" a vector of cluster indexes that are empty

run = function(x = double(1)) {

res <- membershipList$new()

#' Mass function for modified CRP
#'
#' Computes the mass function for the modified CRP of Miller
#'
#' @param x vector giving cluster membership
#' @param size length of x
#' @param lambda parameter for poisson prior on (number of components - 1)
#' @param gamma parameter for Dirichlet prior on membership probability
#' @param tol tolerance for computing log normalizing constant
#' @param log whether to return on log scale
#'
#' @return a scalar giving the mass function for the cluster membership

dMCRP <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
      x = double(1)
, size = integer()

, lambda = double(0)
    , gamma = double(0)
    , tol = double(0, default = 1e-12)
    , log = integer(0, default = 0)
  ) {
    returnType(double(0))

classSizes <- getClusterSizes(x, max(x))     ## size of each class
    clustList  <- getClusterIndexes(classSizes)  ## list of empty/nonempty indices
    C <- classSizes[clustList$nonempty]          ## vector giving sizes of each nonempty cluster

t <- length(C)                               ## number of parts in the partition
    ## Compute log V_n(t)
log_vn <- logvn(t, length(x), lambda, gamma, tol)

## Compute log kernel of mass function
    logK <- 0
    ## Compute lgamma(gamma)
    lgamma_gamma <- lgamma(gamma)
    for ( j in 1:t ) {
      logK <- logK + lgamma(gamma + C[j]) - lgamma_gamma
    }
    if ( log )
      return( logK + log_vn )
    return( exp( logK + log_vn ) )
  }
)

      2. Set the parameters for the empty cluster to the draw from part (1)

#' Compute log V_n(t) as in Miller and Harrison
#'
#' @param t number of partitions
#' @param n sample size
#' @param lambda mean hyperparameter for poisson prior on k-1
#' @param gamma dirichlet parameter
#' @param tol tolerance for sum
#' @return computation of log V_n(t)
logvn <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
      t      = integer(0)
    , n      = integer(0)
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma  = double(0)
    , tol    = double(0, default = 1e-12)
  ) {
    returnType(double(0))
    thresh <- 1.0 - tol     ## the sum decays faster than the poisson CDF
    ## Number of partitions t must be <= n
    if ( t > n )
      return(-Inf)
    a <- 0.0      ## Previous value of log V_n(t)
    c <- -Inf     ## Computation of log V_n(t)
    k <- 1        ## counter for the sum
    p <- 0.0      ## poisson CDF calculation (to be compared with thresh)
    while ( abs(a-c) > tol | p < thresh ) {
      if ( k >= t ) {
        gamma_k <- gamma * k
        a       <- c
        b       <- lgamma(k+1) - lgamma(k-t+1) - lgamma(gamma_k + n) + lgamma(gamma_k) + dpois(k-1, lambda, 1)
        c       <- logsumexp(a, b)
      }
      p <- p + dpois(k-1, lambda, 0)
      k <- k + 1
    }
    return(c)
  }
)

    return( exp( logK + log_vn ) )

dMCRP <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
      x = double(1)
    , size = integer()
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma = double(0)
    , tol = double(0, default = 1e-12)
    , log = integer(0, default = 0)

    t <- length(C)                               ## number of parts in the partition
    ## Compute log V_n(t)
    log_vn <- logvn(t, length(x), lambda, gamma, tol)
    ## Compute log kernel of mass function
    logK <- 0
    ## Compute lgamma(gamma)
    lgamma_gamma <- lgamma(gamma)
    for ( j in 1:t ) {

    n               <- length(targetElements)
    zparms          <- model$getParents(target)
    lambda          <- values(model, zparms[1])[1]   ## Poisson parameter
    gamma           <- values(model, zparms[2])[1]   ## Dirichlet parameter
    ## Get names of parameters for response variable
    yvar            <- model$getDependencies(target, self = FALSE, dataOnly = TRUE, stochOnly = TRUE)
    yparmsNames     <- model$getParents(yvar, stochOnly = TRUE, omit = target)
    yparmsNames     <- model$getVarNames(nodes = yparmsNames)
    ## get number of components in mixture model
    max_components <- 0

    yparmsClust    <- NULL

hi Ethan,

To restore all parameter values when a subject belongs to an existing cluster, you could do something like this:

nimCopy(from = mvSaved, to = model, row = 1, nodes = clusterParamsToRestore, logProb = TRUE)

where clusterParamsToRestore is a vector of node names (I think this is yparmsClust in your case.)

To revert the parameters for all but the new cluster, you could exclude the new cluster from the clusterParamsToRestore. 

nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = clusterParamsToRestore[-idx], logProb = TRUE)

However, I'm not sure if "-idx" will work in compiled code, so you might need to do something like:

nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = clusterParamsToRestore[1:(idx-1)], logProb = TRUE)
nimCopy(from = model, to = mvSaved, row = 1, nodes = clusterParamsToRestore[(idx+1):P], logProb = TRUE)

and you'd need to protect against cases where idx = 1 or idx = P.

Actually, it might be easier to revert for all of them via nimCopy (including overwriting the one you want to update) and then only for the new cluster, assign the new value back into the model via 
model[[nodeName]] <<- ...
or
values(model, nodeNames) <<- ...

Of course you'd need to have saved the updated value in a temporary variable before it got overwritten in the model by the nimCopy.

Let me know if I'm not quite on target with what you need or you have further questions.

-chris

My understanding of Neal Algorithm 8 is that you need to compute the log probability of being in an existing cluster as well as a new cluster.

#' Compute log V_n(t) as in Miller and Harrison
#'
#' @param t number of partitions
#' @param n sample size
#' @param lambda mean hyperparameter for poisson prior on k-1
#' @param gamma dirichlet parameter
#' @param tol tolerance for sum
#' @return computation of log V_n(t)
logvn <- nimbleFunction(
  run = function(
      t      = integer(0)
    , n      = integer(0)
    , lambda = double(0)
    , gamma  = double(0)
    , tol    = double(0, default = 1e-12)
  ) {
    returnType(double(0))
    thresh <- 1.0 - tol     ## the sum decays faster than the poisson CDF
    ## Number of partitions t must be <= n
    if ( t > n )
      return(-Inf)
    a <- 0.0      ## Previous value of log V_n(t)
    c <- -Inf     ## Computation of log V_n(t)
    k <- 1        ## counter for the sum
    p <- 0.0      ## poisson CDF calculation (to be compared with thresh)
    while ( abs(a-c) > tol | p < thresh ) {
      if ( k >= t ) {
        gamma_k <- gamma * k
        a       <- c
        b       <- lgamma(k+1) - lgamma(k-t+1) - lgamma(gamma_k + n) + lgamma(gamma_k) + dpois(k-1, lambda, 1)
        c       <- logsumexp(a, b)
      }
      p <- p + dpois(k-1, lambda, 0)
      k <- k + 1
    }
    return(c)
  }
)
